target.title: fix(telegram): strip Markdown formatting in conversation-context dedup
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Telegram users would see duplicate assistant messages in the conversation context injected into the model when the assistant's reply contains Markdown formatting characters (**bold**, _italic_, `code`, ~~strikethrough~~, or fenced code blocks).

The root cause: OpenClaw sends replies as HTML (`parse_mode=HTML`) via `markdownToTelegramHtml`. The Telegram Bot API strips HTML tags from the returned `Message.text` field. The channel cache stores this stripped plain text, while the session transcript retains the original Markdown. The dedup function (`resolvePromptContextTextDedupeKey`) compares both surfaces without normalizing Markdown formatting, so messages with Markdown produce mismatched keys and appear as duplicates.

Fixes [#102257](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/102257).

## Why This Change Was Made

PR #100573 added `stripInlineDirectiveTagsForDelivery` to both dedup surfaces, which handles inline directive tags. However, it does **not** strip standard Markdown formatting or fenced code block markers (both `` ``` `` and `~~~` styles), so the mismatch persists for any message that uses Markdown formatting or code blocks.

The fix adds `stripMarkdown` to both dedup key surfaces, layered on top of the existing directive-tag stripping.

## User Impact

- **Before**: Messages containing Markdown formatting (**bold**, `code`, _italic_, ~~strikethrough~~, or fenced code blocks in `` ``` `` or `~~~` style) produce mismatched dedup keys and appear as duplicates in the injected prompt context.
- **After**: Prompt-context dedup matches outbound messages regardless of Markdown formatting differences between the session transcript and the channel cache.

## Evidence

### Unit Tests (15/15 passed)

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  15 passed (15)
```

Test coverage includes:
- Basic Markdown formatting (bold, italic, code, strikethrough)
- Backtick fences with/without language tag, multi-line, non-word info strings
- [P2] Tilde fences (`~~~`) with/without language tag
- [P2] Non-word info strings (c++, c#, .tsx, my-lang)
- [P2] Backtick vs tilde fence consistency
- [P2] Transcript body with fenced code vs Telegram cache body (no fences)

### Contract Dedup Tests (22/22 passed)

```
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  22 passed (22)
```

- bot-handlers.runtime.prompt-context-dedup.test.ts: 15/15 passed
- message-dispatch-dedupe.test.ts: 7/7 passed

### Shared Consumer Tests (TTS) (6/6 passed)

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
```

### Real-Machine Verification (9/9 scenarios passed)

```
 tilde fence + language tag          -> stripMarkdown preserves content, strips fence -> MATCH
 tilde fence, bare                   -> stripMarkdown handles bare ~~~ fences       -> MATCH
 backtick fence, non-word info (c++) -> stripMarkdown strips info string, keeps code -> MATCH
 tilde fence, non-word info (c#)     -> stripMarkdown strips info string, keeps code -> MATCH
 backtick vs tilde, same result      -> both produce identical dedup keys           -> MATCH
 backtick fence, info with dots      -> stripMarkdown handles .tsx info string      -> MATCH
 tilde fence, info with hyphens      -> stripMarkdown handles my-lang info string   -> MATCH
 fenced code block transcript->cache -> dedup keys match after normalization        -> MATCH
 mixed formatting (bold+code+fenced) -> dedup keys match after normalization        -> MATCH
```

## Changes

- `src/shared/text/strip-markdown.ts`: Handle `~~~` fences and non-word info strings in code block regex
- `extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.runtime.ts`: Add `stripMarkdown` to `resolvePromptContextTextDedupeKey`
- `extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.ts`: Add `stripMarkdown` to `normalizePromptContextTimestampText`
- `extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.runtime.prompt-context-dedup.test.ts` (enhanced): 15 unit tests including tilde fence and non-word info string regression tests

## AI-assisted checklist

- [x] Marked as AI-assisted in the PR title (`[AI]`)
- [x] Evidence section with validation

## Related

- #100573 (directive-tag dedup fix — partial solution)
- #99117 (closed as completed)
